roundReason: Implementing round 5 answered the four findings of the review at 355ffe8e. All four fixes hold. An adversarial sentence sweep by a reviewer subagent, checked against the code and by a stub run, found that my round-3 finding (1b) was too narrow, plus one further minor wording error.

keyFindings.description: The page says only a *second* stop can cut the trap short. cleanup() is the EXIT trap and restores every signal's default as it starts (3016), whatever started it. So a single stop that reaches the sequence while a trap started by a failed step or the work's end is running also ends it part-way. The trap can run for a long time: the diagnostic reads, a 6-31 s foreground delete, and a Service wait of up to 60 s. 'Send one stop and let the trap finish' then implies that one stop is always safe. Measured 2026-10-25 with the same stub, its work ending in `false`: one `kill -TERM -- -<pid>` during the trap printed `cleanup: start` and nothing after; the no-stop control printed `cleanup: delete done` and `sequence: exit 1`. My round-3 finding asked only for the second stop, which was too narrow.

'For the runs that took the label path, nothing they printed shows when the stop landed relative to the create's request and answer' is too broad for the label-path runs that found nothing. The server answers a create only after storing it, and no Job of theirs was left, so their empty label delete shows the stop landed before the create's answer. What stays unknown for them is before the request left versus in flight; for the two that found a Job, in flight versus after the answer (as 3171-3172 already says). This wording was my own round-3 suggestion.
